clue.text: Assume responsibility for appropriate debt

parts.note: to appropriate something is to take it for yourself
a charge is a sum owed, a debt laid on an account

explanation.surface: Someone shoulders a liability that properly belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective (suitable debt) but is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume responsibility is to step in and direct matters, an idiom for leading.

clue.text: Repeatedly to beat the boy is pointless

indicators.note: pointless means a compass point, here E for east, is taken away

parts.note: Rob is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone thinks beating a boy again and again achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' looks like a moral verdict; it removes E, a compass point, from THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulse is to beat rhythmically again and again, as a heart does.

clue.text: Mistress looked after char

parts.note: kept means maintained, looked after
a char or charwoman is a British cleaning lady

explanation.surface: A lady of the house took care of the cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' is British for a cleaning woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover financially supported by a man is a mistress.

clue.text: Cloth neckwear

parts.note: the cloth is the clergy collectively, so this is the neck garment worn by them

explanation.surface: A fabric scarf or tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloth' looks like fabric; 'the cloth' means the priesthood.
explanation.definitionFit: The white band worn by priests round the neck is clerical neckwear.

clue.text: Exam ended and part corrected

indicators.note: part signals that only a portion of the run exam ended is used

explanation.surface: The exam is over and partly marked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amended has been revised to remove errors.

clue.text: Go on leave

parts.note: to go away on a holiday break, read as a phrasal verb of escape

explanation.surface: Take time off.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape on holiday is to leave for a break.

clue.text: Cuckoo-pint — a sort of drink

parts.note: rum is a kind of spirit, a sort of drink

explanation.surface: A wild flower's odd name is compared to a kind of beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo-pint' looks like it belongs with 'drink' (a pint), but it is the common British name for a wild woodland plant, also called lords-and-ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo-pint is a folk name for the wild lily of that genus, a synonym for the plant.

clue.text: Money for an animal's head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front part, so only the opening of the animal's name is kept

parts.note: a rhinoceros is a large horned animal

explanation.surface: Cash is offered for a beast's head, as a trophy bounty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British slang for cash, of uncertain origin.

clue.text: Specially devised by physician for the mad king at Glamis

indicators.note: mad suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Macbeth, the mad king at Glamis Castle, gets a doctor's special prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamis is the Scottish castle linked to Macbeth.
explanation.definitionFit: In pharmacy a magistral remedy is one prescribed and compounded for a particular patient.

clue.text: Disregard for others' feelings shown by those who are stuck up?

definitions.text: Disregard for others' feelings shown by those who are stuck up?

parts.words: Disregard for others' feelings shown by those who are stuck up?
parts.note: stuck up read literally: people with their arms raised in a holdup have lifted palms

explanation.surface: Snobs show contempt for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' looks like snobbish; it also means hands held up in surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Overbearing arrogance that ignores others is the bossy manner described.

clue.text: Charged in full

explanation.surface: Someone is billed for the whole amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charged is filled up, and so is a thing that is full; both senses mean stuffed or sated.

clue.text: This is never Lily's work

parts.note: recalls the Sermon on the Mount: consider the lilies of the field, they labour not, neither do they spin

explanation.surface: Someone named Lily is accused of never doing her own work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name; it is the biblical flower that does no labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labouring is the activity the biblical lilies never do.

clue.text: Bay from dog creating din inside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the dog word, splitting it after its fourth letter

parts.note: bow-wow is a child's word for a dog

indicators.note: creating suggests the letters of din are made into something new, an anagram

explanation.surface: A dog barks up a racket indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a dog's howl, matching 'dog' and 'din'; it is the projecting window. 'creating' rearranges din, and 'inside' splits the child's word for a dog to take it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a window that projects outward from a wall, the same structure as a curved projecting window.

clue.text: Sounds of merriment in form, forsooth!

explanation.surface: An archaic exclamation is said to be laughter in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' links the two: the second sense is the Scottish exclamation, an interjection like 'forsooth!' expressing surprise or impatience.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud laughs are sounds of merriment; separately, a Scots interjection of protest serves like the old exclamation forsooth.

clue.text: Member in deep sleep in the interval

indicators.note: in places the member's abbreviation within the word for deep sleep

parts.note: a coma is a deep unconsciousness, a deep sleep
M is the abbreviation for Member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A politician dozes off deeply during the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interval' looks like a theatre break; in music a comma is a tiny interval between two notes almost the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory the comma names a minute difference in pitch, a technical interval.

clue.text: Bird on a metal ring is crowing

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a hoop is a ring, often of metal, round a barrel

explanation.surface: A rooster perched on a hoop crows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crowing' fits the cock in the surface, but it means exulting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowing means boasting in triumph, as does being jubilantly elated.

clue.text: A boring book, say, for a dealer in chemicals

parts.note: dry means dull, boring

indicators.note: say signals that the book's name is spoken, its silent first letter dropping out

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms

explanation.surface: A tedious volume is offered to a chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: PSALTER spoken aloud loses its silent P, giving SALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A drysalter was a trader in dyes, gums and preserving salts, an old trade name for a chemicals merchant.

clue.text: The weaker batsmen have no call for getting fit

parts.note: in cricket the tail is the weaker batsmen at the end of the order
O looks like nought, zero, no
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: Lower-order cricketers have no need to get in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting fit' looks like exercise; it is cutting clothes to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor adjusts garments to fit the wearer, the craft of making clothes fit.

clue.text: Impress Tory writer

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the party called Tory
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A Conservative author makes a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' looks like making an impression; here it means to force someone into service.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to compel into military service, the same as enlisting by compulsion.

clue.text: His dealings could be a dire sin

definitions.text: His dealings could be a dire sin

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of dire sin may be turned into something else

explanation.surface: A man's business deals might be a terrible wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Insider dealing is trading on confidential information, a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: One with private company knowledge whose trading on it is illegal.

clue.text: One would be surprised if this were raised

definitions.text: One would be surprised if this were raised

parts.words: One would be surprised if this were raised
parts.note: the facial feature lifted when someone shows astonishment

explanation.surface: Someone would be astonished if something were brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift the hairy arch above the eye in surprise.

clue.text: Train a bit

explanation.surface: Someone is told to coach a little.
explanation.definitionFit: To train soldiers is to exercise them in routine; a boring tool's bit is the tip that makes holes.

clue.text: Girl divorced from a rich man

indicators.note: divorced from means split away, so the letter a is parted from the girl's name

parts.note: Angela is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman leaves a wealthy husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a divorce; the 'rich man' is a theatrical backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy financier who backs a stage show is called by that heavenly name.

clue.text: Interminable old man's tactless remark

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for an old man

explanation.surface: An elderly man's endless indiscreet comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder such as an indiscreet comment.

clue.text: Tower used by some skiers

parts.note: read tower as one who tows, not a tall building: water-skiers are pulled along by a fast motor vessel

explanation.surface: A tall structure serves skiers, like a ski-jump tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' rhymes with 'power' here, not 'flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast motor vessel tows water-skiers, so it is literally a thing that tows them.

clue.text: An old groom showing this animal

explanation.surface: An elderly bridegroom reveals a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a bridegroom; in old use a tiger was a small liveried servant who rode behind a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy in livery attending a carriage was so called; the big striped cat is the animal.

clue.text: Careless cavalier

explanation.surface: A dashing horseman is accused of negligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a casual, brusque manner lacking proper attention or courtesy.

clue.text: Said to be studying architectural decoration

indicators.note: said tells us the word for studying is heard, not spelt

parts.note: reading is studying, as at university

explanation.surface: A student is said to be learning about building ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Reeding is a moulding of parallel convex ribs, like bundled reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental moulding of narrow parallel ridges is a decoration on columns and furniture.

clue.text: Bird, not very big, killed by another

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for very big is removed

parts.note: the osprey is a fish-eating bird of ...
OS stands for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A small bird falls victim to a larger one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird, not very big' reads as a small bird; it is OSPREY minus OS (outsize).
explanation.definitionFit: An animal hunted and slain by another creature is a quarry or victim.

clue.text: Demerara causes guns to go off in drunken bar row

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged guns inside the rearranged bar row
drunken signals the letters of bar row are reeling into a new order
guns going off are fired, and their letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: In a boozy pub brawl, shots ring out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' rearranges bar row and 'go off' rearranges guns, which goes into a gap in the first. Demerara is a coarse cane product from Guyana.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a type of golden-brown cane sweetener, named after a region of Guyana.
